title: Handle the edge case first
idea: The guard goes at the top: check the edge case before the normal work, so the risky step never runs on bad input. Reading and ordering.

exercises.prompt: Where should the edge-case guard go in a plan?
options: At the very start, before the normal work
exercises.explanation: Check the edge case first. Then the normal code only runs when the input is safe.

exercises.prompt: Order a safe plan for 'share the bill among diners'.
blocks: If zero, say no one to share with
Otherwise divide the bill by diners
exercises.explanation: Guard the zero divisor first, then divide only when it is safe.

exercises.prompt: If you divide first and check for zero afterward, the program may already have crashed.
exercises.explanation: Yes - the crash happens at the division. The guard must come BEFORE the risky step to help.
diners is 0, so the guard fires first and the unsafe division (in the else) is skipped.
diners is 3, so the guard's condition is False and the normal branch runs safely.

exercises.prompt: Order a safe plan for 'average = total / count'.
blocks: If zero, say there is no average
exercises.explanation: The zero guard protects the division. This is the same shape every edge-case plan uses.

exercises.prompt: Why does the guard being first actually protect the program?
options: The risky step is skipped whenever the edge case is true
exercises.explanation: When the guard is true, its branch runs and the risky branch is skipped entirely. Order is the protection.

exercises.prompt: A guard-first plan means the normal division only runs when the divisor is safe.
exercises.explanation: Exactly. The else (normal) branch is reached only when the guard found no problem.

exercises.prompt: A problem has an empty case AND a normal case. The clean shape is...
options: if (edge case): handle it; else: do the normal work
do the work, then maybe check
exercises.explanation: Guard the edge case in the if, do the normal work in the else. One tidy if/else handles both.

exercises.prompt: The rule of thumb for edge cases:
options: Check the edge case first, then do the normal work safely
Skip the guard to save time
exercises.explanation: Edge case first, normal work second. That ordering keeps the risky step from ever running on bad input.
